title: JetBlue shares soar after it vows to return to profitability
article:
(Oct 28): JetBlue Airways Corp reassured Wall Street that it’ll be profitable next year, as the debt-laden carrier seeks to overcome persistent losses and high oil prices to prevent a deeper restructuring.

Chief executive officer Joanna Geraghty reaffirmed the company’s confidence in achieving operating profitability in 2027 and delivering at least US$1 earnings per share and positive free cash flow in 2028 in its third-quarter (3Q) earnings report.

“Despite significant fuel headwinds and a challenging summer operation, our revenue performance is among the strongest in the industry,” Geraghty told analysts on a conference call on Tuesday. She added that JetBlue has “multiple avenues” to strengthen liquidity to bridge the carrier to 2028, such as aircraft financing.

JetBlue rose 20% to US$2.86 as of 11am New York time, with other US major carriers seeing fractional or single-digit gains. The stock had sunk to its lowest level on record on Monday before the earnings report was released, sliding by as much as 18%.

The results underscore how soaring jet fuel prices are eating into airline profits despite resilient demand for travel. JetBlue’s more profitable rivals — such as Delta Air Lines Inc, American Airlines Group Inc and Southwest Airlines Co — all cut their profit outlooks in recent weeks. That signalled that even carriers better insulated from war-related spikes are being squeezed.

See also: IndiGo, Air India to shift some flights to new Mumbai airport

The future outlook is a rare bright spot for the New York-based carrier this quarter. JetBlue anticipates a negative operating margin of 4.5% to 6.5% for 2026, compared with the average analyst estimates for a loss of 5.8%, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. It had previously guided for an operating margin loss of 2% to 5% for the full year. The metric represents the percentage of revenue left over after paying operating costs.

The company reported an adjusted 3Q loss of 60 cents a share, missing Wall Street estimates for a loss of 55 cents a share.

The report comes at a critical moment for JetBlue, which is saddled with roughly US$9 billion in debt. A group of creditors, including holders of US$2 billion in bonds due 2031 and a US$742 million first-lien loan, was working with restructuring advisers PJT Partners and Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld. Wall Street has been watching JetBlue closely ever since Spirit Airlines shut down earlier this year.

See also: VietJet faces aircraft, cash seizures in FitzWalter debt fight

“Debt investors continue to price in a default on its loyalty-backed debt and its convert,” TD Securities analyst Tom Fitzgerald wrote in an Oct 26 note to clients. “Credit investors expressed concern that incremental financings are akin to ‘robbing Peter to pay Paul.’”

Geraghty told analysts “there’s a significant disconnect” between the narrative in the bond market and what JetBlue’s financial results are demonstrating. The conference call ended abruptly after a technical issue.

JetBlue also faces elevated costs and intense competition. The airline has posted six consecutive years of operating losses. The last profitable year on an operating basis was 2019, when operating income was about US$800 million.

“Guidance is for an inflection in free cash flow at the end of 2027, though the company will need to reduce burn significantly prior to that target,” George Ferguson, a Bloomberg Intelligence senior industry analyst, said in a research note on Monday. “Its outlook for 4Q appears challenging.”

M&G Real Estate buys Melbourne build-to-rent property for A$215 million
article:
M&G Real Estate, a unit of global savings and investment company M&G, has purchased Bowen Crescent, a new completed build-to-rent (BTR) development in Melbourne, Australia, for A$215 million ($194 million).

The deal marks real estate investment manager’s foray into the Australian BTR sector, bringing assets under its Asia Living Property strategy to around US$500 million ($640 million). The portfolio now spans multi-family housing, purpose-built student accommodation, land lease communities and senior living.

Located close to the Melbourne CBD, the 17-storey Bowen Crescent has 215 one-, two- and three-bedroom rental apartments. There are also co-working facilities, a gym, a swimming pool, sauna and cold plunge.

It is a 150m away from Anzac Station, offering convenient access to the business district, major employment centres, and higher education hubs.

The acquisition builds on M&G Real Estate’s existing strategic partnership with Australian developer and asset manager Novus to develop purpose-built rental housing in Australia.

Demand for professional managed rental housing in Australia continues to grow, supported by strong demographic trends, said Jing Dong Lai, CEO of chief investment officer of M&G Real Estate Asia.

title: Fewer luxury non-landed residential deals as China's tax crackdown dampens sentiment: Huttons
article:
Singapore’s luxury non-landed housing market saw more muted activity in 3Q2026, as uncertainty brought on by China’s campaign to tax offshore wealth weighed on buyer sentiment.

In July, Chinese authorities announced a new 20% income tax on dividends and interest gained from offshore trusts, with a 90-day transition period for voluntary disclosure and settlemetntthat ended on Oct 22.

With the new rules, transferring a property into an offshore trust or income derived from an offshore trust "will be treated as income under the individual income tax law and will be taxable”, explained Mark Yip, CEO of Huttons Asia.

The new regulations have prompted uncertainty in the past weeks as China’s wealthy sought clarifications on potential tax liabilities. Amid this stir, Singapore’s luxury condo market saw fewer transactions, according to Huttons.

Transaction volume of luxury non-landed homes

Luxury non-landed residential transactions totalled 66 deals in 3Q2026, declining 16.5% from 79 the previous quarter and falling 18.5% from 81 deals a year ago, based on data compiled in Huttons’ third quarter Prestige Report.

Huttons defines luxury non-landed homes as private residential units in the Core Central Region (CCR) with a strata area of 2,000 sq ft and above that transact for at least $5 million.

Luxury condo units sold in 3Q2026 had a total sales value of $509.6 million – a 24.3% decline from $673.4 million in 2Q2026 and 31.2% lower y-o-y.

Number of ultra-luxury non-landed homes ($10 million and above) transacted

Ultra-luxury non-landed units — CCR units sized 3,000 sq ft and above that transacted for at least $10 million — saw deals tumble to 11 units during the third quarter, compared to about 24 transactions the quarter before. The figure is the lowest since 4Q2025.

A 3,272 sq ft unit at Sculptura Ardmore that sold for $20 million ($6,112 psf) in September was the most expensive luxury condo deal in the third quarter. The unit at the 36-unit freehold development at Ardmore Park was purchased by an American foreigner.

On the other hand, leasing momentum rose in the luxury non-landed segment, which Huttons attributes to ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNWIs) seeking safe havens like Singapore.

Rental volume rose by 11.2% q-o-q to 727 units in the third quarter, based on Huttons’ basket of luxury non-landed projects. The stronger demand bolstered rents, which increased 7.2% q-o-q.

Top 10 non-landed ultra-luxury homes sold in 3Q2026 by quantum

Seven GCB deals in 3Q2026

In the Good Class Bungalow (GCB) market, an estimated seven deals were recorded in 3Q2026, compared to eight the previous quarter.

This brings GCB deals to 24 for the first nine months of the year, two short of the 26 deals across the same period in 2025. In terms of sales value, the GCBs sold in the first three quarters fetched $880.2 million, 5% lower $927.2 million for the first nine months of 2025.

Top deals in GCB areas in 3Q2026 by price

Leasing activity also picked up in the GCB market, with rental volume jumping 50.6% q-o-q to an estimated 86 transactions. They included a GCB at Tanglin Hill leased for $108,888 per month – the first six-digit monthly rent recorded since 3Q2024, according to Huttons.

In the coming months, UHNWI buying sentiment will likely stay muted amid ongoing uncertainty from the tax crackdown, said Huttons CEO Yip.

“However, selective activity is being sustained by ongoing court-ordered state auctions of luxury apartments tied to the $3 billion money laundering investigation, which continue to draw opportunistic interest,” he added.

In any case, Singapore’s underlying market fundamentals remain resilient. “The strong pre-launch response for rare large-format units in The Park Residence (a 43-unit ultra-luxury project debuting in 4Q2026), paired with attractive entry opportunities from state-led auctions, underscores enduring long-term confidence in the nation's premier residential real estate,” Yip said.

title: ‘Supply onslaught’ to weigh on HDB resale market in 2027, but cash-rich buyers to support prices
article:
Despite an influx of supply, the HDB resale market could see modest price growth next year, supported by the “return of cash-rich buyers”, according to research by Realion (OrangeTee & ETC) Group.

In a 2027 outlook report on the HDB market published on Oct 26, the firm noted that resale flats will see an “onslaught of supply” next year and beyond, as more flats reach their minimum occupation period (MOP).

At the same time, recent policy changes could prompt more private homeowners to return to the HDB resale market.

In August, the government removed the 15-month waiting period for private housing owners looking to buy a non-subsidised HDB resale unit. This is expected to lead to more resale flat transactions, particularly for five-room, jumbo and executive resale flats.

“Cash-rich buyers will likely buy larger resale flats, as they are accustomed to spacious homes,” said Christine Sun, Realion’s chief researcher and strategist.

In addition, legislation lowering the consent threshold for collective sales of older developments was passed in September, potentially spurring en bloc activity. That would “unlock windfall gains for many private homeowners” that could fuel more big flat and million-dollar transactions, Sun added.

The opposing supply and demand factors will likely result in modest growth in resale flat prices next year, on the back of steady transaction volumes.

Realion estimates resale flat prices could grow between 2% and 4% in 2027, more than the 0% to 1% growth it is projecting for the whole of 2026. Resale flat volume in 2027 is expected to come in between 26,000 and 28,000 transactions, on par with its projection for this year.

Projected HDB resale volume and price trends for 2027

More MOP and BTO flats

Around 18,900 flats are expected to reach their MOP in 2027, nearly 5,500 more than the roughly 13,400 flats this year.

In addition, Realion projects almost 100,000 flats to reach their MOP between 2026 and 2030, and around 180,000 flats within the 10-year period from 2021 to 2030. The latter represents a 50% surge over the 120,000 flats that reached their MOP in the preceding decade.

The Build-to-Order (BTO) and Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) pipeline is also anticipated to remain robust, with around 22,000 to 26,000 BTO and SBF units projected to launch next year.

The pipeline, coupled with the recent increase in the income ceiling for BTO flats, could divert potential resale flat buyers to the primary market, where flats are generally cheaper.

In August, the monthly household income ceiling for eligible families buying BTO flats was raised from $14,000 to $16,000. “After the policy changes, we anticipate more buyers purchasing BTO flats instead of resale flats,” said Sun.

Two-speed market to intensify

Given the anticipated rise in demand from cash-rich buyers and the incoming supply of flats reaching their MOP, Sun believes the resale price gap between mature and non-mature estates could widen in 2027, intensifying a “two-speed” HDB resale market.

Median resale flat prices in mature estates rose by 9.6% in 2024 and 8.1% in 2025, outpacing the 6.4% and 5.2% gains recorded in non-mature estates for the same years. “This marked a reversal from 2022 and 2023, when non-mature estates recorded stronger price growth,” said Sun.

Looking ahead, she expects the price gap to expand. With cash-rich buyers “paying top dollar” for premium flats in established neighbourhoods, prices in mature estates are expected to see further growth, supported by more million-dollar transactions.

On the other hand, non-mature estates will likely see smaller and older flats come under pressure as supply increases, escalating competition among sellers. As such, resale prices there could stagnate, with some locations potentially seeing price corrections.

Slowing market

Realion’s outlook for 2027 comes amid a slower year for the HDB resale market. “Buying activities slowed noticeably in 2026, as sellers faced intense competition from a steady stream of BTO flats and a supply onslaught of resale flats reaching their MOP,” said Sun.

Nearly 13,500 flats are expected to have reached their MOP by the end of 2026, almost double the 6,973 flats last year.

New BTO supply has also remained consistent. Including the year's last BTO exercise coming up in November, Realion estimates 19,614 units will have launched this year, compared to 19,723 units last year.

Amid the surge in resale flat supply and competition from the BTO market, the HDB Resale Price Index posted its first quarterly decline in nearly seven years at the start of the year, falling 0.1% q-o-q in 1Q2026.

It eased further in the subsequent quarters, declining 0.3% and 0.1% in the second and third quarters, respectively.

However, premium resale flat deals continued to climb, with 4,607 flats sold for at least $800,000 in the first nine months of the year. They included 1,497 homes that fetched at least $1 million and 12 units sold for $1.6 million or more.

title: How Chinese home-tech brands are making Singapore homes smarter
article:
Singaporeans are no strangers to paying for convenience. In a city where work, family and everyday responsibilities compete for time, we have long looked for ways to make daily life a little easier, whether that means having dinner delivered after a long day at work or groceries arriving at the doorstep.

Increasingly, that same expectation is shaping the home.

We are seeing technology move beyond helping people complete household tasks towards taking more of those tasks off their hands altogether.

For example, robot vacuums no longer just clean floors. More advanced models can map the home, navigate around obstacles, empty their own dustbins and double up as mops that can even wash themselves.

Connected-home technology can automate everything from lighting and curtains to security, reducing the number of small interactions homeowners need to think about each day.

A new generation of Chinese home-tech brands is finding a place in Singapore homes, signalling changing consumer expectations of the technology they live with.

From more features to less effort

For homeowners, the appeal of automation is not necessarily the technology itself. It is what that technology can give back.

Take cleaning as an example. Brands such as Ecovacs have steadily expanded what a robot vacuum can take care of independently, with advanced models offering functions such as intelligent home mapping, automatic dustbin emptying and self-cleaning mopping.

On Lazada, we have seen shoppers increasingly gravitate towards premium, self-maintaining robot vacuums.

Flagship products in this tier have gained a disproportionate share of demand within the robot vacuum category, suggesting that consumers are not only embracing automated cleaning, but are increasingly investing in products that can take more of the work off their hands.

The same desire for simplicity is appearing elsewhere in the home.

Aqara, for instance, offers connected products spanning lighting, curtains, sensors and security that can work together around household routines. Instead of managing each device individually, homeowners can set up routines that take care of small actions automatically.

Individually, these are hardly the biggest demands on our day, but anyone who has come home after a long day to floors that still need cleaning, rushed out wondering whether the lights were switched off or questioned halfway to work whether they locked the door knows how quickly the small things add up. They do not just take time. They take up headspace too.

That is where we see the definition of convenience evolving. The question is becoming less about "What can this device do?" and more about "What will I no longer need to do?"

Winning a place in the home takes more than technology

With more brands and products to choose from, getting consumers to consider something new is not simply a matter of offering more features.

Singapore shoppers have no shortage of choice. While brand recognition matters, particularly for higher-value purchases, consumers today are doing their homework before deciding what deserves a place in their homes.

Our 2026 eCommerce Savvy Shopper Report: Southeast Asia , developed jointly by Lazada and Cube, found that nine in 10 Southeast Asian shoppers frequently check product reviews and ratings, while seven in 10 research products beyond the platform.

This gives brands an opportunity to be considered for what their products can offer, rather than on familiarity alone.

We are seeing this play out among Chinese home-tech brands such as Ecovacs and Aqara, which have developed increasingly sophisticated products spanning automation, connectivity and functionality at different price points.

Ecovacs today ranks among the top three robot vacuum brands on Lazada Singapore, with its self-emptying and self-mopping flagship models among the most searched in the category.

Aqara has carved out a similarly strong position in the connected-home space, growing its footprint across lighting, curtains, sensors and security.

The increasing popularity of such products points to growing interest in what these brands have to offer.

However, there is a danger in equating a smarter home with simply having more technology.

For most homeowners, the goal is not to build the most technologically advanced home possible. It is to make everyday life easier.

A good place to start is therefore not with the product, but with the problem.

What is the repetitive task or small frustration you would most like to remove from your day? From there, consider how much attention the technology will still require after it is set up, whether it pairs with devices already in your home and whether you will actually make full use of the additional features you are paying for.

After all, a feature only creates value if it makes life meaningfully easier.

Making smarter choices in a crowded market

As home technology becomes more sophisticated, choosing the right product can also become more complicated.

A robot vacuum, smart lock or connected lighting system can represent a significant investment, and homeowners must weigh price, features, compatibility and whether a product will genuinely make everyday life easier.

E-commerce has made that comparison easier. On Lazada, for example, shoppers can compare brands, specifications and reviews, and purchase through official brand stores on LazMall.

During our recent 9.9 Mega Brands Sale in Singapore, more than three in four orders came through LazMall, reflecting the importance of trusted channels.

For homeowners, smarter choices go beyond prices and specifications. Check official brand stores, read ratings and reviews, and look into warranties, returns and after-sales support, particularly for higher-value purchases. These provide a fuller picture of ownership long after delivery.

Brands such as Ecovacs and Aqara show how expectations are changing across automated cleaning, lighting and security.

But the smartest product is not necessarily the one with the longest list of features. It is the one that fits naturally into the realities of your life and seamlessly takes a task off your plate.

Because for a busy household, sometimes the most valuable thing technology can give us is not another feature. It is one less thing to think about.

title: GLS plots at Chuan Grove and former Raffles Town Club site released, can yield 930 and 250 residential units
article:
Two residential sites under the Reserve List of the 2H2026 Government Land Sales (GLS) Programme have been released for sale.

The sites, located at Chuan Grove and Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road are available for application and can potentially yield about 930 and 250 residential units, respectively, said URA in an Oct 27 release.

A Reserve List site will be launched for public tender only when a developer has submitted an indicated minimum price that is acceptable to the government.

The Chuan Grove site is a 99-year leasehold residential plot with a site area of 341,170 sq ft and a maximum gross floor area (GFA) of 852,932 sq ft.

The Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road plot, which is the former Raffles Town Club site, is zoned residential with commercial on the first storey. The 99-year leasehold plot, measuring 122,573 sq ft, has a maximum GFA of 257,408 sq ft. This includes up to 26,910 sq ft of commercial space, which must include a supermarket of at least 10,764 sq ft.

Neither of the sites are likely to be triggered for sale, said Mark Yip, CEO of Huttons Asia. Developers may choose to wait for the 1H2027 GLS Programme with the expectation that the sites could be shifted to the Confirmed List, he added.

"While both plots have their own merits, we do not expect them to be triggered for sale in the near term," commented Wong Siew Ying, head of research and content at PropNex.

Chuan Grove site

The Chuan Grove site is close to two other pots that were awarded last year to a joint venture between Sing Holdings and Sunway Developments (now Sunway MCL).

The developers plan to amalgamate the parcels, which will be the site of One Chuan Grove, a 99-year leasehold, 1,056-unit residential project planned for launch in February 2027, said Yip.

The project will add “ample supply” in the Chuan Grove area, leaving “little incentive for developers to trigger the site”, he added.

However, if tendered, he believes the site could fetch a top land rate of $1,300 to $1,400 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr). Sing Holdings and Sunway had paid land rates of $1,376 psf ppr and $1,331 psf for the two site s at One Chuan Grove.

Developers will likely monitor the take-up of the new project to gauge the area’s depth of demand, added PropNex's Wong.

Nearby, Kingsford Group’s 916-unit Chuan Park was launched in November 2024. The 99-year leasehold project occupies the former Chuan Park site that the developer purchased en bloc for $890 million.

The new Chuan Park is 99% taken up at an average price of $2,594 psf, based on lodged caveats as of Oct 27.

Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road site

The Plymouth Avenue/Dunearn Road site is a regular-shaped plot formerly occupied by Raffles Town Club. The club's lease for the land expired on Oct 17.

“It has attractive site attributes, being across from the Stevens MRT interchange station for the Downtown and Thomson-East Coast Lines,” said Wong.

It is also close to schools, including the Singapore Chinese Girls’ School and St. Joseph’s Institution; the National University of Singapore (Bukit Timah Campus), and Singapore Botanic Gardens.

Still, Wong believes incoming supply from other Core Central Region GLS sites that have been awarded, but not yet launched, will deter developers from triggering the site for sale.

The plots — comprising sites at Bukit Timah Road , Dunearn Road, Holland Plain, Peck Hay Road and River Valley Green — could potentially add over 1,700 new homes in the CCR, she noted.

title: Mushrooms, timber, upcycling and old buildings: PLP Architecture's quest for greener, more liveable spaces
article:
Mushrooms might seem an unlikely candidate for the next generation of sustainable building materials, but researchers are exploring how fungi could help reduce the carbon footprint of construction.

Mycelium, the root-like network of fungi, currently has potential applications in insulation, acoustic panels and internal partitions in buildings.

Among those experimenting with it is PLP Labs, the research and strategy arm of UK-headquartered PLP Architecture, which has been developing lightweight mycelium building blocks.

Reinforced with timber dowels and grown in biodegradable formworks, the blocks are still in the R&D stage, although prototypes have been showcased at exhibitions and events.

"More people are becoming aware of the potential of using biomaterials, including materials that can be grown, to reduce embodied carbon," says Tina Qiu, partner at PLP Architecture.

"They are also trying to source locally, which can lower emissions from transportation. Such materials may be more adaptable and better suited for the local environment."

Mycelium is just one avenue of research at London-based PLP Labs, whose work also spans other sustainable materials, circularity, and how the built environment can affect people’s health and well-being.

These interests also inform the firm's architectural projects around the world — from minimising the carbon footprint of construction to adapting existing buildings for new uses.

In Singapore, PLP's portfolio includes the completed Park Nova ultra-luxury condo on Tomlinson Road, as well as the upcoming The Clifford development in Raffles Place and the redevelopment of the Marina Square complex on Raffles Boulevard.

Speaking to EdgeProp Singapore , Qiu discusses which ideas and innovations are already finding their way into buildings, which are still being studied, and what could help bring more of them into wider use.

Growing the next generation of building materials

PLP Labs' experiments with mycelium biocomposites, conducted over three years, began on a small scale.

In a meeting room converted into a makeshift lab at the firm's London headquarters, an interdisciplinary team grew hundreds of fungal samples.

The initial experiments involved growing and casting mycelium into cubes and other simple geometric shapes, before the team tested how it bonded with organic materials such as wood and muslin cloth.

"We experimented with a lot of different fungi and found one that was able to cling onto timber dowels, which gave the blocks their structural integrity," Qiu says. The timber dowels provide internal reinforcement, helping create blocks that are sturdy yet lightweight.

The research took an encouraging turn when it became apparent that mycelium could be grown within biodegradable 3D-printed wood formworks into countless, complex shapes.

"The formwork can be printed from 3D printers using timber substrate, and a bio-based resin glue is able to hold it together," Qiu notes.

With this new technique in hand, the team put different mycelium samples through compression and bending tests at an engineering lab at the University of Cambridge to assess their strength.

By Clerkenwell Design Week in London in 2023, the research had yielded an installation, named Symbiocene Living, comprising 84 mycelium blocks grown over three months. The modular pieces could be arranged in infinite configurations, including as partitions, seating, planters and tables.

PLP subsequently showcased its innovative 3D-printed wood and mycelium technique at other major design festivals and events, including the RHS Chelsea Flower Show in 2025.

Held in London, the flower show featured mycelium columns developed by PLP in collaboration with landscape design firm Modular. The columns were grown entirely using recycled material salvaged from previous shows.

How far can mycelium go?

Besides being biodegradable and carbon-efficient, mycelium also has fire-resistant, insulating and sound-absorbing properties, as well as a high strength-to-weight ratio.

This versatility offers potential applications, including as insulation, acoustic panels, lighting fixtures and internal partitions — mainly in non-load-bearing capacities.

Other architects and designers around the world have likewise been exploring mycelium as a potential building material through temporary structures and installations, such as bio-bricks grown from corn stalks and mushrooms, and mycelium panels on timber frames.

Although its applications in the built environment are still limited, Qiu sees the gradual adoption already as a significant step forward.

Further R&D is needed to expand the use of mycelium in architecture and construction, particularly for external facades and structural components, to help steer the industry away from fossil fuel-based materials.

Although PLP has tested mycelium extensively in the UK, the firm has yet to trial its blocks elsewhere to understand how they behave in other environments.

“There has been interest to bring it to this part of the world [in Asia], but we haven’t had a purpose to bring it here yet,” Qiu says.

Engineered wood in buildings, from Rome to South Korea

Fungi may hold promise for the future of construction, but another natural material — timber — is already being used in buildings across the globe .

In particular, mass-engineered timber (MET) has become a more established alternative to conventional concrete and steel.

Its use can reduce embodied carbon, shorten construction times and add visual richness through timber’s natural grain, colours and textures.

MET comprises engineered wood products with improved structural integrity. It includes cross-laminated timber (CLT), which is made by bonding layers of timber at right angles.

Two examples of PLP’s work with engineered timber are developments currently in the pipeline: the new headquarters for Italy's Ministry of Environment and Energy Security in Rome, and the upcoming National Meteorological Center in Daejeon, South Korea.

In Rome, the 30,000 sq m (322,917 sq ft) building will have two CLT volumes with exposed timber interiors, a rooftop timber canopy embedded with solar panels, a biophilic ground floor and a full-height landscaped atrium.

The South Korean project combines CLT with recycled low-carbon steel in a hybrid structure to reduce embodied carbon, alongside passive shading and earth ducts. It is set to become the country’s first net-zero government building.

Understanding timber's natural ageing

In Singapore, the tropical climate affects how and where timber can be used in buildings, especially if it is exposed to the elements. This also means that greater care is often needed to maintain it.

Heavy rain, intense sunlight and humidity can change timber’s appearance over time. Termites may also be a concern if the wood is not properly maintained.

Still, Qiu emphasises that timber can withstand outdoor conditions without necessarily compromising its performance.

"The durability, robustness and structural integrity are completely there [and unaffected]. It's more of an aesthetic thing," she says.

For example, birch wood’s pale, creamy hues may gradually deepen to richer amber or golden-brown tones after prolonged exposure to sunlight and air. Harsh rain can also leave timber looking greyish.

Some people mistake these changes for signs of deterioration or structural damage, "but it’s absolutely not", Qiu notes.

Others may feel uncomfortable with the visual effects of weathering. "But it's a natural material… Pianos, violins — they all age naturally," she adds.

"I think, over time, people will become more aware that biomaterials have to be allowed to behave and age in their own way."

The Clifford: Integrating timber into its design

With Singapore’s weather conditions in mind, she reckons indoor and sheltered spaces are better suited to timber’s use in the city-state for now.

At The Clifford, an upcoming office and retail development in Raffles Place by Singapore Land Group (SingLand), PLP is introducing MET within glass-enclosed spaces or "floating boxes" at the tower's sky terraces. Timber is also planned for parts of the ceilings.

Meanwhile, the ground-level podium will feature mineral materials such as glass-reinforced concrete, which is significantly less carbon-intensive than standard concrete.

"The floating boxes will be constructed out of timber, which will not be directly exposed to the outside environment but are still very connected to the outdoor spaces and gardens at the sky terraces,” Qiu says. "That combination of timber and greenery is part of the focus on well-being."

A redevelopment of the former Clifford Centre , the 35-storey The Clifford brings together workplaces, health and well-being, sustainability and public life in the heart of the CBD, according to PLP.

"Incrementally, we’re seeing a shift. In Park Nova, there was no timber. In The Clifford, there’s a small amount of timber," Qiu says.

"We hope that in the next project we can bring in more timber into these environments."

Finding new value in old materials

Even as PLP explores alternative building materials, it is also finding ways to give existing structures and materials a new lease of life — including at its own office.

Last year, the firm relocated its headquarters to a larger, 22,850 sq ft space at The White Chapel Building in east London. PLP Labs spearheaded the research and strategy for the new studio’s design.

The team applied a circular fit-out approach, taking every opportunity to reuse, upcycle, repurpose and extend the life of materials.

Over the years, PLP had accumulated plenty of architectural samples — including glass, terracotta and metal components — from their projects.

"Every time we worked on a building, we would have hundreds of samples of glass to make sure it goes on the facade correctly," Qiu says.

"We also had a lot of terracotta tiles, as well as window and door assembly parts like knobs."

Instead of throwing the samples away, PLP worked with suppliers to crush them into aggregates. These were then embedded into terrazzo-style surfaces, such as worktops, in the new office. Repurposed marble was also transformed into new tables.

"So we can see these materials around us as we’re working. They give us a connection to the buildings we’ve designed, which is very unique and special to us," she adds.

PLP estimates that 92% of the materials from the previous headquarters were either reused or donated, while a further 7% was recycled. Only 1% was discarded.

The project diverted waste from the landfill, which saved 175.78 tonnes of carbon dioxide, according to the firm.

It also says it achieved a 75.4% reduction in embodied carbon as compared to conventional approaches to office design and renovation. The project turned out 68% cheaper than the cost of a typical London fit-out, too.

Where new furniture was needed, circular design principles likewise guided PLP's selection of materials.

"The new cabinets and shelves are made out of timber," Qiu says. "They are also movable, not fixed, so that we can be more flexible with the space later on without having to dismantle and reassemble them."

Marina Square: 'Good bones' stand the test of time

In Singapore, PLP is looking to apply similar principles to Marina Square’s redevelopment.

SingLand is partially redeveloping and repositioning the 9.2ha mixed-use complex into a 24/7 destination with residential, hospitality, office, retail, sports, wellness and culture components, designed by PLP and Singapore’s DP Architects.

Slated for completion by 2031, the project will include three new towers — a luxury condo, a mixed-use block with a new hotel and offices, and a serviced apartment block — alongside the existing trio of hotels.

At the same time, the four-storey shopping mall will undergo an asset enhancement initiative.

Qiu points to the value of a well-designed, future-proofed structure that allows a building to be adapted for new uses decades later.

She highlights this forward thinking in Marina Square, originally designed in the 1980s by the late American architect John Portman, who pioneered soaring multi-storey interior atriums and massive self-contained complexes.

"Some buildings, particularly those from the 1980s, had more future-proofing and were ahead of their time in terms of being well thought out and having good structures. They could be used for the long term," Qiu shares.

On that note, she says Marina Square’s retail podium has "good bones for additional interventions", with generous floor-to-ceiling heights that allow for different kinds of innovative spaces to be created within it.

The existing structure of the mall will thus be retained and adaptively reused with minimal demolition. New construction will be limited only to small zones that are necessary for future-proofing.

"That means we can reduce a huge amount of carbon because we don't have to demolish the building and dispose of it later,” Qiu adds.

Making every resource count

The team is also studying how they can recycle and upcycle materials stripped out of Marina Square’s mall — such as glass, partitions and furniture — as much as possible, while applying lessons from their London office redesign.

Among the possibilities being explored is adding recycled glass aggregates and terracotta fragments as accents in mineral-based materials.

Each of the three new towers may then have a slightly different accent in their facades and panels.

"But the base materials will still be mineral ones, which helps reduce embodied carbon. And we're trying to stay away from using metals," Qiu says.

"So the same principles in materiality are holistically applied to the Marina Square precinct masterplan."

While making better use of existing structures and resources is key, they must go hand in hand with efforts to lower operational emissions.

This could include designing efficient building systems and selecting materials that help enhance energy performance, such as facade glazing that minimises solar heat gain to reduce the need for air-conditioning.

"We have to consider both [materials and operations] in parallel," Qiu notes.

Patience to experiment and innovate

Across its research and projects, PLP continues to push the boundaries of what architecture can achieve, pursuing innovations to create more sustainable, healthier, vibrant and comfortable spaces.

Progress may come in small steps, but Qiu believes it is important to take the time to get things right — especially when working with alternative or experimental materials.

For instance, PLP Labs’ work on mycelium building materials has already made “quite a huge progression”, she says.

"From the outside looking in, things may seem to be moving quite slowly. But every step is very purposeful."

title: Seven Hillview Terrace factories up for tender at $51.6 mil; four more on sale for $33.6 mil
article:
A portfolio of seven terraced factory properties in Hillview Terrace within Bukit Batok have been launched for sale by public tender.

The adjoining 999-year leasehold properties — located at 36A, 36B, 38, 38A, 38B, 38C and 38D Hillview Terrace — have a guide price of $51.6 million, said Colliers in an Oct 27 release.

The plots span a combined site area of 31,199 sq ft, which means the price works out to about $1,655 psf on the land area.

While the plots are zoned for residential use under the URA Master Plan, they have been approved for general industrial use. They have a gross plot ratio of 1.62.

Buyers may acquire the site for continued industrial or warehousing use. As privately held factories, they are not subject to JTC approval.

Alternatively, the site’s underlying residential zoning allows developers the option to explore redevelopment.

Subject to approval, an additional 0.30 plot ratio may be granted for the site for residential redevelopment. This would raise the maximum allowable plot ratio to 1.92, Colliers added.

“The flexibility to retain the existing industrial use or explore future redevelopment should appeal to a broad range of owner-occupiers, investors and developers,” said Steven Tan, executive director for capital markets and investment services at Colliers.

The tender for the portfolio will close at 3pm on Dec 1.

Separately, Colliers is also marketing another group of properties in the area. Comprising four freehold semi-detached factories at 31, 33, 35 and 35 Annex Hillview Terrace, the portfolio is up for sale by private treaty with a $33.63 million asking price.

The four properties occupy 19,781 sq ft of residential land with a gross plot ratio of 1.62. Similar to the properties up for sale by tender, the site could potentially qualify for an additional 0.30 if redeveloped for residential use.

Together, the two portfolios represent around 50,980 sq ft of land.

The availability of the freehold portfolio gives buyers “another option to consider alongside the tender site”, said Tan. “For developers, the combination of contiguous land, residential zoning, and long leasehold and freehold tenures creates an opportunity that is difficult to replicate in the area.”

The latest industrial transaction in Hillview Terrace was the sale of a 999-year factory with a land area of 5,672 sq ft that fetched $8.5 million, or $1,499 psf.

Before that, two 999-year factories changed hands in April: One occupied a 6,836 sq ft site that fetched $9.3 million ($1,360 psf), and another, a 4,150 sq ft site that was sold for $5.8 million ($1,398 psf).

Racemic ketamine is generic, a US Schedule III controlled substance, and its dissociative effects could invite prescribing restrictions in outpatient settings.

title: Why Smart Investors Buy Small-Cap Stocks (And Why Big Funds Can’t)
article:
Small-cap stocks
– companies with a market capitalisation below S$1 billion, often sitting around S$400 million to S$500 million – might look like peanuts next to giant Singapore blue-chip banks.
Yet, these smaller companies represent some of the most compelling opportunities in the market.
Because fewer people follow them, they often sit as hidden gems right under our noses.
The Big Fund Dilemma
Why don’t managers of multi-billion-dollar funds scoop up these bargain small-caps?
Imagine you are hosting a dinner party for a thousand guests.
You can only choose restaurants massive enough to seat a thousand people.
There might be a fantastic little restaurant around the corner charging a fraction of the price with food just as good as a five-star hotel’s, but you simply cannot go there with a thousand people.
Fund managers face the exact same structural limitation.
They manage billions of dollars.
Even if a fund manager bought an entire S$200 million company outright, it wouldn’t move the needle for their total portfolio.
As retail investors putting S$10,000, S$20,000 or S$30,000 into the market, we don’t have that handicap.
We can comfortably hold
blue chips
and real estate investment trusts (REITs) while taking full advantage of the neglected smaller companies big funds are forced to ignore.
Simple Businesses Beat Opaque Financials
Analysing a small-cap is no different from evaluating a large-cap: you are buying a piece of a business.
In fact, small-caps are often much easier to understand.
Major financial institutions can act like complex sausage machines – money goes in, something complicated happens inside, and profit comes out the other end.
Their annual reports run to hundreds of pages, and what happens behind closed doors can be opaque even to seasoned analysts.
Compare that to a small consumer business selling everyday snacks like curry puffs.
Aside from the secret recipe, there is no mystery inside the business model, and the financial statements are straightforward to digest.
The Misconception About Size and Risk
Many investors assume large companies are inherently safe and small companies are inherently dangerous, but size alone is no shield against distress.
A massive property developer carrying billions in debt can go under during a downturn, whereas a cash-generative small-cap sitting on a net-cash balance sheet cannot easily go bust.
Furthermore, heavy analyst coverage does not make a large-cap stock safe, as analysts often herd together to avoid standing out from the crowd.
Finally, while trying to call the CEO of a major bank for a quick chat will get you nowhere, management at a small-cap is far more accessible to interested shareholders wanting to understand the operations.
Market volatility affects all share prices, but fundamental business risk diminishes the better you understand what you own.
Get Smart: Conviction Beats Market Volatility
Small-cap investing gives retail investors a distinct structural edge over institutional players.
By focusing on simple,
cash-generative businesses
with strong balance sheets, you can spot value long before the rest of the market catches on.

title: Nvidia vs AMD: Which Chip Stock Is the Better Buy Today?
article:
Nvidia
(NASDAQ: NVDA) and
AMD
(NASDAQ: AMD) are two of the leading players in the market for advanced AI chips.
Yet, their business models, profitability and valuations differ.
Nvidia is the more established – and far larger – company.
As of 16 October 2026, it had a market capitalisation of US$5.2 trillion, compared to AMD’s US$863 billion.
But there are benefits to being a challenger, and both companies have been swept up in the enthusiasm for
all things AI
.
Nvidia: The Dominant Player
Nvidia is the undisputed market leader in graphics processing units (GPUs), each of which can have many cores that allow for processing of complex operations simultaneously, making them suitable for training the large language models (LLMs) that are the foundation of generative AI.
Notably, Nvidia also owns the CUDA computing platform, which allows developers to use GPUs for general-purpose processing, and not just the graphics rendering they were traditionally designed for.
Many developers in AI have been trained to use CUDA, which only works with Nvidia chips, creating a barrier to entry for other chip companies.
Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary of the
AI boom
– its revenue rose by 3.5x to US$216 billion in its financial year ending January 2026 (FY2026), compared to FY2024.
Its margins are equally impressive, with a gross margin of 71% in FY2026. The company also generated nearly US$103 billion in cash from operating activities in the same year.
Part of this windfall has gone into investments and partnerships with key players in the AI ecosystem, from frontier labs OpenAI and Anthropic, to AI data centre operators such as
CoreWeave
(NASDAQ: CRWV).
Some market participants have likened these arrangements to circular financing, since all are important Nvidia customers.
Related articles:
Amazon and 2 Other Winners: 3 Growth Stocks to Buy Now and Hold for the Long Term
More Than Just Chips: Why the AI Revolution Needs These 5 Companies
AMD: The Upstart
AMD’s traditional strength was in making central processing unit (CPU) chips, which were initially overlooked when the AI boom first started.
However, the increasing focus on inference and AI agents means that demand for CPUs is expected to increase by 10x from 2025 to 2030.
Indeed, Muse. from
Meta Platforms
’ (NASDAQ: META), and OpenAI’s Dots, the two companies’ respective AI agents, both run on AMD’s EPYC-branded CPUs.
AMD is also challenging Nvidia in the GPU space with its Instinct product, which it is combining with its CPUs, networking, and ROCm software stack to create Helios, its fully integrated AI infrastructure offering.
Unlike CUDA, AMD’s ROCm is open-source and can run on GPUs from other manufacturers, even Nvidia’s.
If ROCm is able to attract more developers and users, it may even be able to breach the CUDA moat.
Hyperscalers from Meta to
Microsoft
(NASDAQ: MSFT) are spending huge sums of money on AI chips and looking for alternatives to Nvidia so it doesn’t exercise excessive market power.
This presents AMD with an opportunity to take market share from the leader.
Related articles:
3 US Stocks That Doubled in a Year: Should You Buy, Hold or Take Profits?
5 AI-Related Growth Stocks to Supercharge Your Investment Portfolio
Which Chipmaker Has the Stronger Business?
For now, Nvidia is still far ahead of AMD, which had US$35 billion in revenue for its financial year ending December 2025 (FY2025), 1.5x its FY2023 revenue.
But this was still just 16% of Nvidia’s top line for the comparable period.
Both have data centre businesses that are growing strongly.
In Nvidia’s most recent quarter, 2QFY2027, its data centre revenue grew by 2.2x to US$89 billion on strong demand for its cutting-edge Blackwell chips.
AMD’s data centre business experienced similar levels of year-on-year growth, with the segment’s revenue of US$6.7 billion being 2.1x the year-ago figure.
Yet, Nvidia’s business is far more profitable, a reflection of its market leadership.
For example, its 1HFY2027 net income margin was 66%, compared with AMD’s 17% for 1HFY2026.
Despite its market leadership, Nvidia isn’t resting on its laurels.
Earlier this year, it announced the Vera CPU, purpose-built for agentic AI, which it claims is twice as efficient as, and 50% faster than traditional CPUs.
Still, the desire from hyperscalers to see a viable alternative supplier to Nvidia should ensure that AMD gets its share of AI-driven demand.
AMD also stands to benefit from operating leverage, as fixed costs are spread across a larger business.
Its gross profit margin rose from 40% in 2QFY2025 to 54% in 2QFY2026, and is expected to reach 56% in 3QFY2026.
Looking ahead, both businesses must continue to innovate to stay ahead of the competition.
Size also gives Nvidia the advantage here.
In 1HFY2027, it spent US$13.4 billion on R&D, nearly 3x the US$4.9 billion AMD spent in its equivalent period.
It’s also worth noting that Nvidia’s R&D expenditure was just 7.5% of revenue over that period, compared to 22.6% for AMD.
Valuation and Risk
Given Nvidia’s superior economics, one might expect it to attract a premium valuation to AMD.
However, this is not the case.
Nvidia’s forward price-to-earnings ( P/E) ratio is 24.9x, while its PEG ratio (which accounts for expected earnings growth) is 0.5x.
The equivalent figures for AMD are 39.5x and 0.6x respectively.
Part of the explanation for this paradox is that AMD has already seen a significant run-up in its share price – it is 137% higher in the year to 16 October 2026.
Nvidia’s share price, in contrast, rose by just 13% over the same period.
Although both companies face similar risks, including the bursting of the AI bubble and the cyclicality of the
semiconductor industry
reasserting itself, AMD’s higher valuation also means that it is more susceptible to changes in investor sentiment.
Nvidia, meanwhile, might be doubly exposed to the underperformance of the companies in the AI ecosystem it has invested in.
In the past week, for example, CoreWeave’s share price has fallen by 24% as investors fret over its debt levels and ability to scale its business.
Get Smart: Which AI Chip Stock Would I Buy?
Nvidia and AMD offer two distinct ways to invest in the growth of AI computing.
Nvidia benefits from its established leadership, strong software ecosystem and proven profitability.
AMD offers the potential for significant growth and operating leverage if it successfully expands its market share.
However, given its superior economics and lower valuation, Nvidia might be the pick between the two, despite understandable scepticism about how much more a US$5.2 trillion company can grow.

Option #1: Invest S$10,000 in an ETF
ETFs are baskets of stocks that track specific market indices or themes.
For example,

ETFs lower the research burden because they simply hold whatever stocks are in the index they track and need little upkeep from you.
Investors should, however, watch out for fees and expense ratios, along with exchange rate fluctuation risks if they are investing in overseas ETFs.
Additionally, watch out for concentration risk.
The three local banks make up about 58% of the STI, so ES3 is heavily tied to the banking sector.

title: JetBlue shares soar after it vows to return to profitability
article:
(Oct 28): JetBlue Airways Corp reassured Wall Street that it’ll be profitable next year, as the debt-laden carrier seeks to overcome persistent losses and high oil prices to prevent a deeper restructuring.

Chief executive officer Joanna Geraghty reaffirmed the company’s confidence in achieving operating profitability in 2027 and delivering at least US$1 earnings per share and positive free cash flow in 2028 in its third-quarter (3Q) earnings report.

“Despite significant fuel headwinds and a challenging summer operation, our revenue performance is among the strongest in the industry,” Geraghty told analysts on a conference call on Tuesday. She added that JetBlue has “multiple avenues” to strengthen liquidity to bridge the carrier to 2028, such as aircraft financing.

JetBlue rose 20% to US$2.86 as of 11am New York time, with other US major carriers seeing fractional or single-digit gains. The stock had sunk to its lowest level on record on Monday before the earnings report was released, sliding by as much as 18%.

The results underscore how soaring jet fuel prices are eating into airline profits despite resilient demand for travel. JetBlue’s more profitable rivals — such as Delta Air Lines Inc, American Airlines Group Inc and Southwest Airlines Co — all cut their profit outlooks in recent weeks. That signalled that even carriers better insulated from war-related spikes are being squeezed.

See also: IndiGo, Air India to shift some flights to new Mumbai airport

The future outlook is a rare bright spot for the New York-based carrier this quarter. JetBlue anticipates a negative operating margin of 4.5% to 6.5% for 2026, compared with the average analyst estimates for a loss of 5.8%, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. It had previously guided for an operating margin loss of 2% to 5% for the full year. The metric represents the percentage of revenue left over after paying operating costs.

The company reported an adjusted 3Q loss of 60 cents a share, missing Wall Street estimates for a loss of 55 cents a share.

The report comes at a critical moment for JetBlue, which is saddled with roughly US$9 billion in debt. A group of creditors, including holders of US$2 billion in bonds due 2031 and a US$742 million first-lien loan, was working with restructuring advisers PJT Partners and Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld. Wall Street has been watching JetBlue closely ever since Spirit Airlines shut down earlier this year.

See also: VietJet faces aircraft, cash seizures in FitzWalter debt fight

“Debt investors continue to price in a default on its loyalty-backed debt and its convert,” TD Securities analyst Tom Fitzgerald wrote in an Oct 26 note to clients. “Credit investors expressed concern that incremental financings are akin to ‘robbing Peter to pay Paul.’”

Geraghty told analysts “there’s a significant disconnect” between the narrative in the bond market and what JetBlue’s financial results are demonstrating. The conference call ended abruptly after a technical issue.

JetBlue also faces elevated costs and intense competition. The airline has posted six consecutive years of operating losses. The last profitable year on an operating basis was 2019, when operating income was about US$800 million.

“Guidance is for an inflection in free cash flow at the end of 2027, though the company will need to reduce burn significantly prior to that target,” George Ferguson, a Bloomberg Intelligence senior industry analyst, said in a research note on Monday. “Its outlook for 4Q appears challenging.”

title: Wee Hur secures lease extension for Tuas View dorm
article:
Wee Hur Holdings has secured a lease extension of two years and eight months from JTC Corporation for its Tuas View Dormitory.

The extended lease for the 15,744-bed dormitory will be valid from Nov 1 to June 30, 2029.

Tuas View Dormitory first began operating in 2014 as Wee Hur’s first purpose-built workers’ dormitory and is held through a joint venture where Wee Hur has a 60% interest. The dorm is operated by the group’s joint venture partner, TS Group.

The dormitory reported an average occupancy rate of 92% in 1HFY2026 ended June 30 with “steady” rental rates. It already meets the interim standards under the Dormitory Transition Scheme, which all dormitories are required to meet till 2030.

According to Wee Hur, the extension provides continued income visibility for its workers’ dormitory business. Revenue for the business was up by 50.7% y-o-y to $63.3 million in 1HFY2026, supported by the first full half-year contribution from the 10,500-bed Pioneer Lodge.

“The extension of Tuas View Dormitory reflects the trust built over more than a decade of operating one of Singapore’s largest workers’ dormitories. It gives us continued income visibility from an established asset and reinforces our workers’ dormitory business as a stable source of recurring income for the group,” says Goh Chengyu, CEO of Wee Hur Property.

See also: Mapletree Investments completes transition to self-management of UK student housing assets

Shares in Wee Hur closed 2 cents lower or 3.39% down at 57 cents on Oct 27.

title: Whirlpool cuts outlook again on lacklustre demand, soaring costs
article:
(Oct 27): Whirlpool Corp slashed its full-year outlook for the third time this year and forecast its first annual loss in decades, citing a sluggish consumer environment and high commodity prices.

Whirlpool now expects ongoing loss per share of US$1.30 for 2026, down from its previous forecast of ongoing earnings per share of US$2.50 to US$3. The original guidance provided in January was for ongoing EPS of US$7.

Sales declined for a fourth straight period in the third quarter, dragged by “softer industry demand” in North America and economic challenges “that undoubtedly intensified over the last three months,” Chief executive officer Marc Bitzer said on Tuesday morning’s earnings call.

Whirlpool shares dropped as much as 16% in postmarket trading on Monday, before bouncing back as much as 6.6% on Tuesday morning in New York.

The fridge and microwave maker is cutting costs and increasing prices to improve margins, but higher steel, resin and base metal costs, as well as tariffs, countered these gains, chief financial officer Roxanne Warner said on the call.

See also: US stocks get tech boost as Anthropic files for IPO

“While we made progress on our pricing and cost takeout actions, this progress was partially offset by higher raw material, fuel, and logistic costs,” Bitzer said.

Consumers are still holding back on replacing their appliances, according to Bitzer, though new premium products launched this year are doing well even in a soft discretionary market.

While “outsized” price increases are needed to offset higher costs, they could lead to share losses, RBC Capital Markets analyst Mike Dahl wrote in a post-earnings note. The outlook also does not account for potential disruption from Brazil’s election, creating further risk for its Latin America business.

See also: US stocks gain as investors parse Anthropic IPO filing

Whirlpool has been working to lower its leverage, but those efforts have been complicated by a depressed US housing market and gloomy consumer sentiment as affordability concerns continue to weigh on spending for home appliances.

Whirlpool now aims to reduce net debt to under US$4.5 billion by the end of the year, a US$500 million improvement from its target announced last quarter.

title: US consumer confidence rises for first time in four months
article:
(Oct 27): US consumer confidence unexpectedly rose in October for the first time in four months on brighter views about the job market and business conditions.

The Conference Board’s gauge increased 7.5 points to 91.7, the highest since June, data released on Tuesday showed. The figure topped all projections in a Bloomberg survey of economists.

A measure of expectations for the next six months rose nearly seven points in October to 72.6, while a gauge of present conditions increased to the highest since April.

“The recovery was in line with retail gasoline prices easing from September to October,” Fergus McCormick, a senior economist at the Conference Board, said in a statement. “Yet, despite the increase in October, consumer confidence remained on the long-term downward trend that’s persisted over the past few years.”

The survey showed more Americans see business conditions as good rather than bad, while the share who see jobs as plentiful rose to a six-month high.

See also: US new home sales fall amid surge in mortgage rates

Despite the increase in confidence this month, consumers remain troubled by the impact of higher prices on their budgets and on wage growth that is lagging behind inflation. Borrowing costs have also climbed more recently, making homes, vehicles and other big-ticket purchases less affordable.

With the midterm elections a week away, affordability remains a defining issue for voters and their assessment of the economy. However, Americans are more sanguine about the job market as lay-offs remain historically low.

The confidence survey showed the difference between those saying jobs are plentiful and those indicating they are hard to get — a metric closely followed by economists to gauge the job market — improved.

See also: US orders for durable goods increase by most in five months

Plans to buy big-ticket items were mixed, while vacation intentions edged lower. However, sentiment has been a poor indicator of personal spending, which has been resilient and continues to underpin economic growth.

“The labor market remains supportive of spending activity,” Ben Ayers, a senior economist at Nationwide, said in a note. “The trend in consumer surveys remains soft but that hasn’t stopped households from maintaining a solid pace of purchases.”

Over the past six months, consumers younger than 35 and those making US$100,000 ($128,041) or more expressed greater confidence. In October, sentiment improved across all political groups, particularly Republicans.

The survey period for the report was Oct 1-21.

The Conference Board’s confidence index generally focuses on labor market conditions, whereas a separate metric of consumer sentiment from the University of Michigan emphasises views about personal finances and the cost of living. Still, they have largely tracked each other in recent years.

The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index, released last week, edged down to a five month low as high prices and rising interest rates depressed morale.

title: US new home sales fall amid surge in mortgage rates
article:
(Oct 27): Sales of new homes in the US edged lower last month as homebuilders’ efforts to trim prices and offer sales incentives failed to offset a surge in mortgage rates.

New single-family home sales decreased 0.6% in September to an annualised rate of 676,000, according to figures released on Tuesday by the federal government. That beat the median estimate of 651,000 annualised sales in a Bloomberg survey of economists.

The median sales price of a new home fell 3.9% from a year ago to US$400,400, the seventh of nine months so far in 2026 to show a year-over-year price decline.

September’s dour sales figures reflect the gravity of the challenges facing the housing market. Mortgage rates rose about a half-point last month — reaching the highest level in almost three years in early October — and have eased only slightly since then. The surge in borrowing costs has sapped demand among would-be homebuyers and helped drive a measure of homebuilder confidence to the lowest level in 14 years.

Entry-level buyers are especially sensitive to increases in financing costs, making builders that cater to them such as DR Horton Inc and Meritage Homes Corp more vulnerable, Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Drew Reading said in research published last week. Builders are struggling to keep customers motivated, offering smaller homes and subsidized mortgage rates to offset poor affordability.

With customer demand so weak, builders have only slowly worked down the supply of new homes on the market. Last month, the inventory of new homes for sale dropped 2.3% from a year ago to 476,000, according to Tuesday’s figures. That represents 8.4 months of supply at the current sales pace, the least so far this year but still well above pre-pandemic levels.

See also: US orders for durable goods increase by most in five months

New-home sales in the South, the nation’s biggest home-selling region, fell 6.6% to an annualised 413,000. Sales in the Midwest also fell, offsetting gains in the West and the Northeast.

New-home sales are seen as a timelier gauge than purchases of existing homes, which are calculated when transactions close. However, the data are volatile on a monthly basis. The government report showed 90% confidence that the change in new-home sales ranged from a 14.4% decline to a 13.2% gain.

title: Anthropic IPO filing calms nerves with signs of healthy growth
article:
(Oct 27): Anthropic PBC set itself a challenge by opening its books to prospective initial public offering (IPO) investors right after a punishing week for the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. When Wall Street took a close look, it generally liked what it saw.

Investors may not have been surprised by the company’s surging revenue, with US$16.3 billion ($20.9 billion) in the first half of this year alone — up more than 1,300% versus the same period in 2025. But they were impressed by the firm behind Claude’s broad and diversifying adoption among business customers, and tolerant of what may be slowing growth.

“To me, what’s more important is that their recurring revenue’s coming from both an increasing number of enterprise customers, and it’s not concentrated,” said Max Gokhman, the head of AI and digital asset solutions at Franklin Templeton, in an interview with Bloomberg News.

About 79% of Anthropic’s revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came from outside the company’s top five customers, according to the filing.

See also: Acts of God meet acts of AI in private equity’s new debt play

Another figure that jumped out to many was the US$131.7 billion of cash and cash equivalents the company had at the end of June. To Yuri Khodjamirian, the chief investment officer of Tema ETFs, that’s surprising for a firm that has only raised US$141.1 billion to date.

“If you just take one number versus the other, that suggests that to date this company has spent US$9 billion basically building this business,” Khodjamirian said. “They have a lot of future commitments to compute, there’s a lot of lease commitments, things like that that come in the future. But that’s quite remarkable.”

“One of the more bullish takeaways is actually this is a profitable business that has a lot of cash on the balance sheet, enough to kind of sustain its growth into the future,” Khodjamirian added. “Which is a very positive sign.”

See also: Meta upsizes equity offering as it seeks almost US$98 bil

The filing helped reinject investor enthusiasm in the AI trade after it took a drubbing over the last two weeks amid concerns about the amount of debt fuelling the infrastructure build-out and how much return the largest companies are seeing about the massive investment in the nascent technology. Monday’s trading offered a calmer backdrop going into a slew of hyperscaler earnings scheduled for this week after Meta Platforms Inc’s huge capital expenditures last week sent investors out of risk assets.

The Nasdaq 100 index gained 1.1% on Monday after two back-to-back weeks of declines. The S&P 500 Index rose 0.7% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which measures chipmaking stocks, gained 2.8%.

“Certainly the Anthropic S-1 has stoked greed a lot more than fear,” said Gokhman of Franklin Templeton. “There’s a lot in that S-1 that’s not super surprising to folks who have been paying close attention, but it kind of confirms the enterprise growth potential. And I think that is probably one of the biggest reasons we are seeing the broader complex of AI-related stocks kind of pick up, since they were the ones that were really getting beaten down over the last couple of weeks, it makes sense that we are seeing that rebound.”

Meta also said on Monday that it had upsized a planned sale of common and preferred stock to nearly US$98 billion, up from the US$95 billion that it had announced ahead of Anthropic’s filing.

“They are smart to say let’s get a bunch of capital while we can because it may feel somewhat expensive today, but if the AI debt fears come true, it’s going to be really expensive next year when they really, really need it,” said Alexander Morris, the chief investment officer of FM Investments. “The concern is being left out, so when someone does something, we have to put our marker in too, just to remind people don’t spend all your money on this flashy new thing.”

Meta shares fell more than 1%, extending a decline from last week. Still, investors see more than enough demand in the market to digest the new issuance with Anthropic’s upcoming IPO.

“There’s going to be more of a differentiated case to make and we will be able to define who are the potential winners and losers,” Gokhman said. “But it’s also way too early to tell, so I think right now holding a diversified basket makes the most sense and then changing your allocations gradually as we see more clarity on who is becoming more dominant in each of the spaces.”

title: Memory stocks lost their shine despite strong earnings
article:
(Oct 27): Sandisk Corp, Micron Technology Inc, Seagate Technology Holdings plc and Western Digital Corp were among the stock market’s biggest winners in the first six months of the year as demand from the artificial intelligence (AI) build out seemed insatiable.

But since then momentum has turned against the shares of AI component manufacturers, like the makers of semiconductors, memory and storage, with investors questioning the durability of massive spending commitments. As a result, Sandisk, Micron, Seagate and Western Digital are in the bottom 10% of the S&P 500 Index in the second half of 2026, and even blowout earnings haven’t been enough to reverse the trend.

“The market is telling you that expectations are changing for how long the earnings boom is going to last for these companies,” said Joe Tigay, a portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments.

This dynamic was apparent last week, when Western Digital’s results and forecast late on Thursday blew past expectations and the company boosted its dividend, but the shares fell 3% on Friday because of concerns that AI spending had peaked. At the end of September, Micron beat projections for profits and revenue and gave an outlook that was far better than expected, but the stock is down 15% since then.

Seagate is the next up, with its earnings due after the close on Tuesday, and analysts expect the company’s net income to triple. Sandisk follows on Thursday, and its earnings per share are projected to soar more than 6,100%.

Shares of Seagate were up 2.3% on Tuesday morning, while Sandisk rose 1.3%, Micron gained 1.5% and Western Digital leaped 4.7%.

See also: Instagram ramps up video strategy in escalating TikTok, YouTube rivalry

“Now that the trade has gotten long in the tooth, what can turn it around?” said Andre Bakhos, president of Ingenium Analytics. “Not only will you need great earnings, but you’ll need to see follow-through next quarter and the one after that.”

This growth is being fuelled by massive spending on AI, which isn’t seen slowing anytime soon. Last week, Meta Platforms Inc boosted its capital expenditure plans for the year. Wall Street anticipates that Microsoft Corp, Amazon.com Inc and Alphabet Inc will affirm or raise their AI spending plans when they report earnings this week. And on Monday, Anthropic PBC filed for its long-awaited initial public offering, which is expected to demonstrate the enduring strength of the AI trade, sending memory and storage stocks higher.

See also: Applied Materials ups stake in BE Semiconductor to about 20%

The problem is investors are becoming increasingly skeptical about the payoff from all this AI spending, particularly now that so much of it is being financed by debt. For example, a gauge of Meta’s credit risk hit a fresh record after the company revealed its projected capital expenditures. Add in a challenging economic backdrop featuring high oil prices and interest rates, and it’s easy to see where the pessimism is coming from.

This helps explain why the once high-flying memory and storage stocks have had their wings clipped. Since the start of the third quarter, Sandisk and Western Digital are down more than 44%, while Seagate has lost 33% and Micron has sunk 22%. While that’s taken a chunk out of their year-to-date gains, all remain up significantly in 2026, led by Sandisk’s almost 430% surge, which is the second-best performance in the S&P 500.

“There used to be this concentrated FOMO mentality surrounding memory, but now investors are starting to weigh the risk of all that expenditure and debate whether it can keep going,” Bakhos said.

In other words, the group needs external validation from the big AI spenders to keep the rally going. If they reassure investors that their plans are leading to profits, confidence in the group should rise because capital expenditures will remain elevated.

“The fundamental story seems largely intact over the near term, but risks are obvious and the bear case remains,” Tigay said. “Should they not live up to expectations, demand could fall off a cliff.”

Seagate and Sandisk are expected to see slowing growth in the coming years, according to analysts’ estimates. Seagate’s revenue is projected to rise about 56% in its 2027 fiscal year, which ends in June, before decelerating to 37% in fiscal 2028 and 20% in fiscal 2029. Sandisk’s revenue for its 2027 fiscal year, which also ends in June, is projected to leap 140%, but the pace is expected to slow to 20% in fiscal 2028, before actually declining 7% in fiscal 2029.

One positive for the group is the shares aren’t expensive. Micron trades at five times earnings estimated over the next 12 months, making it the second-cheapest stock in the S&P 500 after Charter Communications Inc, and Sandisk is close behind at less than six times. Meanwhile Western Digital’s multiple is around 12, and Seagate’s is 15. All are trading at a discount to the broader market, with the S&P 500 valued at roughly 19 times estimated earnings and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index at 20.
